findings.description: Capped at `suspicious` against the tool's highly_suspicious because the per-condition sample sizes are NOT reported -- 15/15/15 is my inference from N = 45 over three conditions. findings.title: Exp3 design sensitivity (Experiment 3, cell sizes)
findings.description: Context, not a defect, and the tool renders no verdict. No study in the paper reports an a-priori power analysis, so there is nothing to reproduce; this is the design-sensitivity question asked of the paper's own cell sizes instead. A 12-versus-12 contrast has under half the sample needed to detect even a large (d = 0.8) effect at 80% power, yet Experiment 3 reports effects several times that size at very small p. Small studies are not wrong, but a significant result from an underpowered design sits exactly where selection inflates estimates -- which is the relevant frame for reading this paper's effect sizes.

No study in the paper reports an a-priori power analysis, so there is nothing to reproduce; this is the design-sensitivity question asked of the paper's own cell sizes instead. A 12-versus-12 contrast has under half the sample needed to detect even a large (d = 0.8) effect at 80% power, yet Experiment 3 reports effects several times that size at very small p. Small studies are not wrong, but a significant result from an underpowered design sits exactly where selection inflates estimates -- which is the relevant frame for reading this paper's effect sizes.

findings.title: Methods typo in outcome definition (Experiment 3, Procedure)
findings.description: A typo in an acknowledgement is nothing; this one is in the sentence that defines the primary outcome measure of an experiment, and it is precisely the sentence that has to be relied on to determine whether the Experiment 3 means of 7.33 exceed their scale. Recorded as evidence that the passage was not closely read, not as an arithmetic problem. The paper also prints 'Fours studies examine' in the Current studies section and 'when participants were under cognitive loaded' in the General discussion.

findings.title: Exp1 main effects self contradiction (Experiment 1, Self-evaluations)
findings.description: The passage claims significant main effects of BOTH cue and direction, prints an F for the cue effect only, and then states that no other main effects were significant -- which contradicts the claim about direction just made. In a 2x2 there are exactly two main effects, so 'no other' can only refer to direction. Unresolvable from the text: no statistic is given for the direction main effect anywhere in Experiment 1.

anchors.quote: A 2(similarity cue: shared birthday vs. different birthday) × 2(direction: upward vs. downward) ANOVA revealed significant main effects of cue and direction of comparison such that those sharing a birthday reported higher self-evaluations (M = 4.92, SD = 1.14) than those not sharing a birthday (M = 3.96, SD = 1.3), F(1, 43) = 7.77, p = .008. No other main effects were significant.

findings.title: Data availability state but withhold (Experiment 3, footnote 4)
findings.description: The paper's only data-availability statement offers the complete data on request rather than depositing it. This is entirely ordinary for a 2011 psychology paper and is not evidence of anything on its own; it is recorded because several of the anomalies above (unreported cell sizes in every study, irreconcilable error df, two unreconstructable cells) are exactly the questions that access to the raw data would settle, and because the article has since been retracted.

findings.title: Authors own multiplicity disclosure (Experiment 4, footnote 5)
findings.description: Recorded as good practice rather than as a problem, and as the reason I did not run multiplicity_report on Experiment 4's contrast family: the authors performed the correction themselves and disclosed which result does not survive it. One contrast drops from p < .05 to p = .13 under Tukey HSD. Experiment 2 carries a parallel footnote. The disclosure is honest and should be weighed against the paper's other reporting problems.
